answersReviewFindings.finding: Finding 1 (role_keep.go:541): retry() returned false whenever ctx had ended, so the handover's own roleKeepHandoverWindow deadline was treated as a shutdown. For a claimed role whose bus stalls the 10-minute window usually ends inside a read, so ten minutes of failure ended with nothing above Debug, where the same failure ending in a pause logged at Error.
answersReviewFindings.fix: retry quiets only cancellation (errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.Canceled)), so a read the deadline cut off keeps its error and ended() returns it. The reviewer's second half, walks a shutdown cancels, is done with one narrowing: after walkKeptRole, a cancelled context is silent only when the walk left no copy forwarded and unconfirmed (new roleKeepDrainResult.unconfirmed, set at the confirm cursor write), because that copy is re-forwarded by the next walk and TestADrainThatEndedBetweenItsForwardAndItsConfirmLeavesTheHolderOneStoredCopy guards it. The doc at :495-499 no longer claims the loop's ctx checks end quietly when they return readErr.

trickyParts: The branch had already merged #2446 in its unsquashed form over five earlier forward merges, so on each conflicting hunk the branch side already contained main's text. That is why eleven of eleven Go blocks resolve as this branch's text whole, and it is a fact about this merge rather than a rule for the next one.

The 20 re-added changelog fragments are the kind of defect no conflict marker shows and no suite catches: the fold would simply have written 27.1.0's entries twice. The file-set comparison against the pre-merge diff is what found them, and it is worth running on every forward merge rather than trusting the fingerprint alone.

The shutdown rule has one exception, and it is load-bearing: a walk that failed at its confirm cursor write leaves a copy forwarded but unconfirmed, so a cancelled handover that did that must still report. Without the exception TestADrainThatEndedBetweenItsForwardAndItsConfirmLeavesTheHolderOneStoredCopy fails.
